prompt.context: Our client is PLD, a global manufacturer of snack foods and beverages. PLD has been a market leader in China's potato chips (PC) market for over two decades but is facing increasing local competition. Most notably this year, the company's volume share in the South China region declined from 60% to 20%, and the company has hired us to find out why and how to react.
prompt.question: Why did PLD's volume share in the South China region decline from 60% to 20%, and how should PLD react?

clarifying_info.q: What is PLD's volume in South China this year?
How are existing competitors WWT and DLT doing this year?
clarifying_info.a: WWT and DLT volumes grew by 10%.
There is one new competitor, XCD, which entered the South China market in the middle of this year (approximately 3 months ago as of September). XCD has generated 280,000 tons of sales since entry.

clarifying_info.q: Why is XCD doing so well?
clarifying_info.a: XCD introduced a baked potato chip product (using minimal or no oil in production), unlike existing fried products from PLD, WWT, and DLT.

clarifying_info.q: What do we know about consumer segments in the PC market?
clarifying_info.a: There are two consumer groups: Totally Fried Guys (TFGs) who prefer fried products, and Completely Baked Dudes (CBDs) who prefer baked/low-oil products. TFGs comprised 80% of total market consumption but more people are switching to the CBD group. Frequency of eating potato chips has not changed for either group.

clarifying_info.q: What is the national PC market structure?
clarifying_info.a: Last year, PLD had 800,000 tons of national sales with 40% market share, followed by WWT (10%, 200,000 tons) and DLT (5%, 100,000 tons). Total national market was 2,000,000 tons. South China accounts for 10% of overall national PC market.
Consumers see current potato chip products as commodities, so average price is similar across competition.

clarifying_info.q: What was last year's South China market structure?
clarifying_info.a: PLD: 60% share, 120,000 tons; WWT: 20% share, 40,000 tons; DLT: 20% share, 40,000 tons. Total South China market: 200,000 tons.

framework: Diagnose root cause of share loss: decompose volume share into client volume vs. market size (Vol. Share = Vol. / Market Size) to determine whether share loss is driven by volume decline, market growth, or both
Understand competitive dynamics: assess existing competitor performance (WWT, DLT) and identify new entrants driving market size change
Analyze the new competitor: quantify XCD's performance, understand their product innovation (baked chips), and assess which consumer segment is driving growth
Assess threat level: evaluate whether XCD is stealing PLD's existing customers (TFG group) or growing the overall market by bringing in new consumers (CBD group)
Recommend strategic response: address both short-term (protect South China / TFG base) and long-term (respond to baked product trend nationally)

questions.prompt: Diagnose why PLD's South China volume share dropped from 60% to 20%. Walk through the math.
questions.guidance: Candidate should decompose share = volume / market size. PLD volume grew ~10% (not declined), so the share loss must come from market size expansion. Candidate should calculate implied market size from PLD's 20% share and 100,000-ton volume, then compare to prior year.

math.setup: Vol. Share = PLD Volume / Total Market Size. Rearranged: Market Size = PLD Volume / Vol. Share. Prior year annualized run-rate by Sept: 120,000 * 9/12 = 90,000 tons. This year PLD: 100,000 tons. PLD growth = (100,000 - 90,000) / 90,000 ≈ 10%. Implied current market size = 100,000 / 20% = 500,000 tons by September.
steps: Last year full-year South China market: 200,000 tons
PLD this year (9 months): 100,000 tons — growth of ~10%
Implied total market this year (9 months): 100,000 / 20% = 500,000 tons
Market growth: 500,000 vs. 150,000 — more than 3x growth in 9 months
Conclusion: PLD's volume was essentially stable; the market exploded in size due to new entrant(s)
math.answer: PLD's volume share dropped because the market size tripled, not because PLD lost customers. PLD volume actually grew ~10%.

questions.prompt: Given WWT and DLT also grew 10%, what does that tell us about who drove the market growth? Quantify the new entrant's volume.
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognize that PLD+WWT+DLT together account for far less than 500,000 tons, confirming a new entrant with massive share. An excellent candidate will calculate XCD's monthly run-rate and compare it to PLD's.

math.setup: Combined volume of PLD+WWT+DLT this year (9 months). Last year SC volumes: PLD 120k, WWT 40k, DLT 40k = 200k total. 9-month equivalent at +10% growth each.
steps: XCD volume: 500,000 - 166,000 = ~280,000 tons (confirmed by interviewer) in only 3 months
XCD monthly volume is more than 8x PLD's monthly volume
math.answer: XCD accumulated ~280,000 tons in just 3 months, running at ~93,000 tons/month — more than 8x PLD's ~11,000 tons/month.

questions.prompt: Why is XCD doing so well? What product innovation did they bring, and which consumer segment is driving their growth?
questions.guidance: Candidate should explore the 4Ps and focus on product. XCD introduced baked chips targeting the CBD (Completely Baked Dudes) segment. The CBD group was only 20% of market volume before but is now more than half. Frequency of consumption has not changed for either group, so the new CBDs must be previous non-consumers of potato chips who were put off by oil in fried products.

questions.prompt: Is XCD a real threat to PLD in the short term and long term?
questions.guidance: Short term: XCD appears to be growing the overall market by attracting previous non-consumers rather than stealing TFG customers from PLD. PLD's volume is stable and TFG user base is intact. South China is only 10% of national market. Long term: The CBD trend is growing, XCD has had massive success, and South China may be only a test market before XCD expands nationally. This represents a significant long-term threat.

brainstorming.prompt: How should PLD react to XCD's entry and the growing baked-chips trend?

categories.name: Short-term (protect TFG base and South China)
ideas: Increase marketing investment in South China to reinforce PLD brand loyalty among TFG consumers
Run promotions (e.g., price discounts, buy-one-get-one) to defend shelf space and purchase frequency
Introduce new flavors or limited-edition varieties to re-excite the TFG segment and drive trial
Increase trade spend with South China retailers to secure preferred shelf placement
Strengthen distributor relationships and distribution coverage in South China

categories.name: Long-term (respond to baked product trend)
ideas: Develop and launch PLD's own baked potato chip product to capture the growing CBD segment
Acquire or partner with XCD to gain their baked product technology and customer base
Conduct R&D to improve baked chip taste/texture to match or exceed XCD's product
Expand baked product launch nationally if South China pilot succeeds
Build marketing around health/wellness positioning to appeal to CBD consumers at scale

categories.name: Monitoring and intelligence
ideas: Track XCD's expansion plans — determine if South China is a test market for a national rollout
Monitor CBD vs. TFG consumer trend data at national level
Benchmark XCD's baked product on taste, price, packaging, and distribution

recommendation: In the short term, PLD's core business is not directly under attack — PLD's volume and TFG user base are stable. PLD should defend its South China position through increased marketing, promotions, and new flavors targeting TFGs while monitoring XCD's next moves.

In the long term, the CBD trend and XCD's explosive growth represent a real strategic threat, especially if XCD expands nationally. PLD should develop or acquire a baked potato chip product to compete in the CBD segment and prevent XCD from establishing a dominant national position.
risks: XCD may expand nationally sooner than expected, rapidly eroding PLD's share in other regions
The CBD trend may accelerate and erode the TFG base, reducing PLD's core market
PLD may be slow to develop a competitive baked product, giving XCD a durable first-mover advantage
Baked product development may cannibalize existing fried product sales
next_steps: Immediately assess PLD's R&D capability to develop a baked chip product; set a target launch timeline
Evaluate acquisition of XCD as an alternative to organic R&D
Increase marketing and promotional budget for South China in the current quarter
Commission consumer research to quantify the pace of TFG-to-CBD switching nationally
